slidetranscripts.slidetranscript: <Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" FirstLineMargin="-27" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="As you learned in Module 1, the CQI process is a cyclical process of problem-solving that requires the deliberate use of data & evidence. To work effectively, the CQI process needs a viable infrastructure within which to function – the CQI process MUST be supported and informed by an effective CQI system which is a coherent set of structures, functions, policies and procedures or system features that facilitate the CQI process." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Finally, you will recall in Module 3, a deep review and practical application of the California 5-Step CQI Process. The process is meant to be revisited as teams learn and refine their work, and it can be initiated at different points depending on what the work requires. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Step 1 Define the Problem. Clarify the Who and the What by clearly defining the focus of the analysis and the population being examined.Step 2 Understand Underlying Conditions. Dig deep to uncover what is causing the problem, using data and root cause analysis to learn why the pattern is occurring.Step 3 Identify a Solution and Plan for Implementation. Select actionable strategies grounded in evidence and develop a plan that fits local conditions and resources.Step 4 Implementation of the Solution. Put the plan into action.Step 5 Test the Solution and Revise Approach as Needed. Evaluate what was implemented, review results and feedback, and make adjustments so improvement is sustained over time.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Module 4, is going to focus on the who. Who from each county will participate in the CQI process and the various venues envisioned to help counties succeed.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Good job! You’ve completed Lesson 1! Let’s check our learning before moving on.Select the button below to start." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Question #2, True or False: County/Tribal FFPS Leadership Teams oversee local FFPS implementation. They bridge state-level guidance with local application, ensuring strategies are tailored to community needs.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Option 1: True
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Option 2: False" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="CDSS has developed a contractual relationship with Chapin Hall to ensure each county/Tribe has the opportunity to recruit, select, and compensate a maximum of three expert consultants. The consultants will participate in the county/Tribal FFPS Leadership Team, Regional Prevention CQI Collaborative, and the county's/Tribe's CQI Implementation Team(s) depending on the array of EBPs included in the county's/Tribe's Comprehensive Prevention Plan." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Expert Consultants is a broad term that encompasses three distinct types of lived experts. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="First, those with personal or lived experience inside the child welfare or probation system. This could be experience as a youth in care (who is now over 18) or a parent or caregiver. Your social workers are going to be critical when recruiting this type of Expert Consultant. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Second, those with personal experience navigating community-based services. These are families who have walked-the-walk, know how to connect others to services, and your more grassroots families. Your community-based provider community, your family resource centers, united way, etc. are likely who you will lean on to recruit this type of Expert Consultant. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Finally, the third type of Expert Consultant are from the Tribal community. The voices from Tribal communities have not been a decision-making tables historically and this effort is striving to ensure they are. Some Tribes may want to officially designate someone as their Tribal Representative while others may not want to be that formal and a Tribal Advocate will be involved in this work. Regardless of who is at the table from the Tribal Community, we are really hoping you can prioritize involving Tribal Partners in this work, if you are not already. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="We are using the term Expert Consultant intentionally, rather than only leaning on the term “lived expert” – Using the term Expert Consultant helps with two important things:
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="1). Helps others in the room begin to “see” them as the experts they are; and 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="2). Helps to normalize that people are bringing way more experience and knowledge to the table than “just” their relevant lived expertise. They bring a wealth of knowledge about how other individuals like them also experienced the system and may also have employment or educational background that can be leveraged." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="All people with lived experience have expertise that is crucial to positively impacting the families and communities we serve.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="With Expert Consultants involved, agencies are more likely to:
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Accurately interpret their data and understand what it really means
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Identify creative, innovative solutions
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Recognize and address real barriers families face
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Build trust with communities
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Remember: Organizational norms should value lived expertise as true expertise - equal to professional credentials.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="When you involve Expert Consultants throughout your CQI work, you gain insights that data alone cannot provide and solutions that are grounded in lived reality.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="These three strategies create the foundation for effective collaboration.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="1. Use Plain Language - This ensures everyone has equal access to information and can participate fully from the start.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Avoid child welfare or probation jargon
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Define all acronyms every time
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Provide context in everyday language so all start with the same understanding
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="2. Address Power Dynamics - This builds trust and creates psychological safety for all participants.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Understand who’s in the room and how prior relationships may impact both parties
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Create transparency in decision-making and leadership opportunities for Expert Consultants
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Model vulnerability and openness to feedback
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="3. Show Impact - This sustains engagement by demonstrating that their voices truly matter and lead to real change.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Share how their input influenced decisions
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Create feedback loops by tracking recommendations and reporting back
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Celebrate when their ideas lead to change
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Creating trauma-informed environments helps Expert Consultants participate meaningfully and comfortably.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Essential Practices:
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Check-ins as needed before, during, and after meetings,
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Breaks especially in longer meetings,
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Safe spaces for questions and learning,
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Choice of when and how to share their story
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Remember:
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Always ask permission before resharing someone’s story, even if it was shared previously,
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Make it easy for people to say “no” and honor their boundaries,
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="View people as whole individuals, not solely defined by their experience
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Personal story sharing should always be voluntary, never a requirement for participation. Focus on creating spaces where people can contribute their expertise in ways that feel safe and authentic to them." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Authentic engagement doesn’t end when a meeting does. Sustained engagement requires ongoing attention, regular communication, and flexibility.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Regular Check-Ins
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Maintain regular check-ins, including prep and debrief for meetings (adapt to individual needs)
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Create relationships where they feel comfortable reaching out
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Express Gratitude
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Ask about their preferences for recognition (public vs. private, formal vs. informal) 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Based on their preferences, consider handwritten notes, public recognition, follow-up calls
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Be Flexible
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Offer flexible meeting times that work with their schedules
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Provide virtual meeting options to reduce travel burdenOffer in-person meetings when feasible and desiredBe understanding of competing priorities and life circumstances
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Show Outcomes
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Follow up to share results from their inputKeep them feeling involved and like they're making a difference
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="While counties may not always be able to provide supports like transportation or childcare, you can demonstrate commitment by being flexible with meeting formats and times, responsive to their needs, and consistently showing how their participation makes a real difference in improving prevention services.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Challenges are normal and expected. The key is addressing them proactively rather than reactively.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="If expert consultants hesitate to speak up - address power dynamics explicitly; use small group discussions first; model vulnerability.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="If leads aren’t sure how to take action based on expert consultant input – be transparent about decision-making upfront; track recommendations; identify quick wins, and keep the lines of communication open.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="If engagement wanes over time – conduct regular check-ins to discuss barriers to engagement; share outcomes consistently; express gratitude meaningfully. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="If staff or partners are resistant to engagement of Expert Consultants – provide training to help staff or partners receive and respond to feedback constructively; focus on continuous improvement.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Use Chapin Hall support and the Working with Expert Consultants guide to troubleshooting section for detailed guidance on common challenges.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="You’re an important component of your county's/Tribe's CQI work and can ensure expert consultants are treated with the respect they deserve.As the CPP &/Or CQI Lead, you are responsible for:Creating welcoming, psychologically safe environmentsSharing how their input influences decisionsModeling authentic engagement for your teamRemember, there is support available:Working with Expert Consultants Guide Chapin Hall consultation and technical assistanceYour role is to create conditions for authentic partnership and support Expert Consultants' meaningful contribution to improving prevention services for families.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="You're the bridge between Expert Consultants and your county's/Tribe's CQI work.As the CPP &/Or CQI Lead, you are responsible for:
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Participating in county or Tribal-specific orientation if offeredCreating welcoming, psychologically safe environmentsSharing how their input influences decisions at your agencyModeling authentic engagement for your teamRemember, there is support available:Working with Expert Consultants Guide Chapin Hall consultation and technical assistance
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="You also have a responsibility to create conditions for authentic partnership and support Expert Consultants' meaningful contribution to improving prevention services for families.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="These five principles should guide all your interactions with Expert Consultants.Remember These Five Essentials:Authentic Engagement is Relational - Build genuine partnerships from the beginningLived Expertise is True Expertise - Value it equally with professional credentialsAddress Power Dynamics - Be transparent and create space for all voicesCreate Safe Spaces - Use trauma-informed practices; never require disclosureShow Impact - Consistently share how their input influences decisionsYour success in working with Expert Consultants will strengthen your county's/Tribe's CQI work and lead to better outcomes for families.Authentic engagement isn't about perfection - it's about connection, transparency, and genuine partnership.Now we will examine each aspect of the county's/Tribe's CQI infrastructure at a deeper level.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Let’s review the role of a county's/Tribe's FFPS Leadership Team if not already in place. Counties may be tapping an existing group like their Interagency Leadership Team (ILT) or Cross-sector Collaborative to meet this need and the leads may differ significantly, take a look at the overarching purpose and objectives for this leadership team and consider the following: 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Where are decisions impacting FFPS implementation made? 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Who should or currently oversees efforts and provides strategic input? 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="How often is progress monitored? 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Where could alignment with other prevention initiatives be strengthened? 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="How can the feedback loop with partners be improved? 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="More information will be shared shortly about the standardized fidelity and outcomes templates and CARES training will provide a deeper dive into accessing reach and capacity reports.” 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Depending on the EBPs included in the counties CPP, team membership will vary. For example, counties may need to include the contract holder of home visiting EBPs like Parents As Teachers, or Healthy Families America. Similarly, counties may need to include a mental health partner that holds the contracts of Functional Family Therapy or Parent Child Interaction Therapy. Or, a county agency may hold provider contracts themselves and may invite CBO(s) to participate. Technology or CARES Liaisons may be an asset if available. Similarly, child welfare and probation program managers or deputy directors in charge of family maintenance, 602, or expectant and parenting youth cases can strengthen messaging and referrals. Compensated lived, community, and Tribal representatives are also critical participants. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Welcome to Lesson 3. Lesson 3 provides an opportunity to define the core aspects of a CQI Data Infrastructure.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Select “Next” to begin." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Let’s unpack what we mean when we say the CQI Implementation Team(s) are responsible for maintaining the CQI data infrastructure. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Data Collection: The systematic gathering of information (reach, capacity, outcome, and fidelity data) to monitor EBP implementation, assess performance, and inform continuous quality improvement.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Data Management: Organizing, storing, and securing data to ensure accuracy, accessibility, and confidentiality throughout the CQI process.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Data Analysis & Interpretation: Examining and making sense of collected data to identify trends, assess outcomes, and derive insights that inform decisions and improvements.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The next series of slides will go into more detail and provide examples of data collection, management, and analysis. Select the ”Start” buttons below to learn more. Several slides are associated with each category.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="This table outlines each of the EBP models, their reporting frequency for state CQI monitoring, and identifies the four models (two are FFT) who have their own data management system and have entered into a contractual agreement with CDSS to generate an annual fidelity and outcomes report for all providers across California. Click on the hyperlink to the CFPIC website to locate a CQI Brief for each of the EBPs that describes in depth each of the outcome and fidelity measures and data collection process. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Functional Family Therapy (FFT) Partners & LLC (both versions of the model) collect and will share data with CDSS.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Homebuilders purveyor stores outcomes data and will report it to CDSS bi-annually. Some of the fidelity data will be reported by the purveyor and some by the provider. The Homebuilders EBP brief specifies responsibilities. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Multisystemic Therapy (MST) similar to Homebuilders, there are some data points captured and reported by the purveyor and some by the provider. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The remaining EBPs will require the county/Tribe CPP/CQI Lead to collect provider outcomes and fidelity data using the standardized report templates also found on the CFPIC website hyperlinked on this slide. The next slide shows how the data will be aggregated and describe the next steps." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The Outcomes Aggregate tab from the PAT Fidelity and Outcome Report Excel Template is depicted here on the screen. Providers will use the template each month to track clinician fidelity and youth outcomes by accessing data from the PAT Penelope or Visit Tracker data system. The aggregate tab will pull data from the outcomes tab. This data should be reviewed and discussed each quarter at the HV CQI Implementation Team. It is important to note, a fidelity and outcomes aggregate tab is included in the same excel template. The county/Tribal CPP/CQI Lead will use this aggregated data to complete the CARES Outcomes & Fidelity Template. More on the next slide.Select the tab below to download the Excel template." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="On an annual basis, the county, Tribal CPP, and CQI Lead(s) will:
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Complete Appendix C: Provider Outcome and Fidelity Template using the year end data captured in the Excel Outcomes Aggregate tab. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Submit the outcomes PDF template to CDSS via email FFPSApreventionservices@dss.ca.gov 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The CDSS FFPS team will upload provider outcomes data into the CARES backend for the county/Tribe. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Counties/Tribes will be able to access a CARES Tableau data set to compare their outcomes with those of other counties. It is important to note, Appendix C in the PAT CQI Brief also includes a fidelity template to report annual data to CDSS. The outcomes template is the only one depicted here.Select the tab on the right to download the PAT CQI Brief." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Data Management refers to organizing, storing, and securing data to ensure accuracy, accessibility, and confidentiality throughout the CQI process. Data management serves as the centralized system that enables consistent access to reliable data for analysis. Proper data management ensures that data remains accurate, accessible, and consistent across counties, creating a reliable source for subsequent analysis. Raw data will eventually be turned into a structured format, making it ready for deeper examination.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="We’re going to talk about three components of data management: Data Entry, Data storage, and Data quality. For reach and capacity data, providers will enter data directly into the CARES Provider Portal on a monthly basis. For outcome and fidelity data, providers and the CPP and CQI Lead(s) or purveyors will use the standardized templates, like the PAT samples we reviewed moments ago, to enter data for each EBP on a biannual or annual basis and then sent to CDSS FFPS team who will upload into the backend of CARES." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Data storage, remember, is another key component of data management. Ensure data is stored securely allows for the data to be extracted for analysis and visualization. The first level of data storage happens locally… at the local level data will continue to be stored by either purveyor or provider-specific data management systems. This data is primarily used by the CPP, CQI Lead(s), EBP providers, and purveyors for local implementation monitoring. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="CARES is the second level of data storage. All EBP data (including reach, capacity, outcomes and fidelity) will be stored (reach & capacity) or uploaded (fidelity & outcomes) into CARES. This centralized storage allows counties and the state to access and use the data for CQI purposes, enabling data aggregation and visualization to support oversight and strategic decision-making." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The last component of data management is data quality. The purpose of data quality is to identify missing or inaccurate data and to maintain high data integrity. Data quality looks different for reach and capacity data versus outcome and fidelity data because of the way that the data is collected and stored. Because reach and capacity data are entered into the Provider Portal, built-in data validation features ensure accuracy, completeness, and quality control, helping to prevent missing or inaccurate data entries. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="More information will be shared in the CARES training depicting data validation mechanisms. For outcome and fidelity data, we’re recommending data validation and quality checks to identify missing or inaccurate data and to maintain high data integrity for the provider and purveyor templates… again to help ensure data accuracy, completeness, and quality prior to being uploaded into the backend of CARES." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The last component of CQI Data Infrastructure is data analysis. Data analysis transforms managed data into actionable insights through system analysis and interpretation. The goal is to extract meaningful information that supports decision-making and continuous improvement. Data analysis and interpretation enable counties and CDSS to make informed decisions, adapt strategies, and implement targeted improvements. It is the ultimate purpose of data collection and management: to gain insights that enhance EBP effectiveness and contribute to positive outcomes for children and families.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The first component of data analysis is data reporting and visualization. Being able to generate data reports and visualize the data is tremendously important in order to start making sense of it. For data reporting, the CARES training will support automated and customizable reports. For data visualization, dashboards (like Tableau) will be used to visualize key metrics in real-time. These dashboards will be integral for making data actionable and accessible to partners, especially the lived experts, at the state and county's or Tribe's level. Again, more information will be available in the CARES training." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Let’s explore data analysis techniques that can be used at both the state-level and the county/Tribal level. At the state-level, data analysis is essential for ensuring consistent, informed decision-making across counties, identifying areas for improvement, and fostering accountability and continuous quality improvement in child welfare services. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Descriptive analysis describes how data will be used to identify trends, compare outcomes across regions, and monitor key performance indicators.Root Cause Analysis is used to identify underlying factors affecting performance, especially for recurring issues. Common approaches include use of a fishbone diagram or answering 5 Whys.Comparative analysis can be used to evaluate county/Tribal-level performance, identify variations in outcomes, and highlight both areas of success and those needing improvement, enabling targeted support and fostering shared learning across counties." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="County or Tribal CQI Implementation Teams will use descriptive analysis of EBP data to identify trends, patterns, and areas for improvement to monitor performance against county's/Tribe's goals and purveyor benchmarks. They will use the CARES dashboards to access real-time updates on their metrics, facilitating quick decision-making at the local level. And they will apply the 5-Step CQI Process to conduct Root Cause Analysis and identify small tests of change." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="This diagram should look very familiar at this point. Module 3 provided a deep dive into each of the 5-Steps. The structured approach guides counties through identifying problems, implementing solutions, and ensuring continuous improvement in the prevention CQI work. Each step is designed to be data-driven and community-focused, ensuring that FFPS CQI efforts are effective and equitable.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Step 1: Define the Problem (Who & What)The first step is to clearly identify who is affected and what issues they face using CARES data. For example, if data shows low engagement in a Home Visiting program among specific racial or geographic groups, the team defines this as the focus of analysis. This ensures the problem is specific and data-driven.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Step 2: Understand Underlying Conditions (Why)The second step is to dig deeper to understand why the problem is occurring through root cause analysis. Continuing with the example, the team might discover barriers like transportation challenges or cultural misalignment. This uncovers the context behind the data.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Step 3: Identify a Solution and Plan for Implementation (How)The third step is to develop evidence-based solutions tailored to the identified root causes. If transportation is a barrier, the team might offer virtual service options or partner with local organizations for transportation support. This keeps the solution focused and relevant. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Step 4: Implementation of the Solution (Take Action)The fourth step is to pilot the solution on a small scale, allowing for real-time monitoring and adjustments. Using the virtual service example, the team may first test it in one rural area before expanding if successful. This minimizes risk and maximizes learning. Stakeholder engagement, including lived experts, ensures solutions are culturally relevant and community-informed.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Step 5: Test the Solution and Revise Approach as Needed (Evaluation & Revision)The fifth step is to evaluate the solution’s impact and make adjustments as needed. In the virtual service example, the team assesses whether engagement increased among rural families. If effective, they can expand the approach; if not, they revisit the root cause analysis.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Equity in Action: An equity lens is applied throughout by disaggregating data to identify disparities. If engagement among rural families remains low, the team explores additional barriers, such as language access or cultural relevance, ensuring context-specific solutions. Involving lived experts validates findings and grounds the data in real-world experiences, making solutions inclusive, culturally responsive, and effective." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Good job! You’ve completed lesson 3! Let’s check our learning before moving on.Select the button below to start." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Question 1, The CFPIC CQI Resources webpage provides access to which of the following resources? 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Option 1: EBP specific CQI Briefs,
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Option 2: Provider Monthly Outcome & Fidelity Excel Templates,
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Option 3: Purveyor/Provider Aggregate Outcome & Fidelity Template for CDSS/CARES,Option 4: Working with Expert Consultants Guide,Option 5: All of the above" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Question #2, True or False: The county's/Tribe's CQI Implementation Team(s) are responsible for data collection, data management, and data analysis/interpretation?Option 1: True,Option 2: False" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Welcome to Lesson 4!
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Lesson 4 provides an overview of the Regional Prevention Continuous Quality Improvement Collaborative, also known as the PCC.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Select “Next” to begin." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The initial county or Tribal technical assistance mechanism will be in the form of regional Prevention Continuous Quality Improvement Collaboratives. The PCC is envisioned as a strategic opportunity for counties to engage in a structured, data-driven approach to improving EBP implementation, enhancing regional collaboration, and promoting shared learning. The PCC is an opt-in initiative, meaning that participation is highly encouraged but not required. It is not a federal CQI requirement, but it provides counties with an invaluable opportunity to enhance their CQI processes and implementation efforts; and learn from other counties or Tribes.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Seven regional collaboratives will meet virtually quarterly in the first year of implementation to review reach, capacity, outcome, and fidelity data strengths and challenges. County/Tribal CPP teams are encouraged to meet in-person and connect virtually with their regional colleagues. Each collaborative will last approximately 4 hours. Members of the county's or Tribe's FFPS CQI team(s), including lived experts and contract holders or providers, will participate in the regional PCC and bring data and brainstorm strategies with their regional colleagues." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Grouping counties by training regions within the PCC framework optimizes support and enhances regional collaboration. Two separate PCC groups will convene specifically for small counties to ensure that the unique needs of small counties are addressed. Small counties face distinctive challenges, such as resource constraints and limited workforce capacity, which necessitate tailored approaches and support structures. Both the Yurok and Karuk Tribes are situated in the Northern Region and are envisioned to join the small northern region counties for the PCC." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Each county/Tribe participating in the PCC will form a team. These teams should include representatives from: 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Compensated Expert ConsultantsCompensated Tribal Representatives/AdvocatesThe county's/Tribe's child welfare and probation department FFPS/CQI lead(s) County/Tribal child welfare and probation administrators EBP service provider contract holders (if applicable) EBP providers (compensated through contractual agreements or memorandums of understanding if feasible) 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="To foster team cohesion and collaboration, it is recommended that counties have all team members convene in the same location to participate virtually in the PCC sessions." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Participation in the PCC provides counties with several key benefits, including: 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="A structured venue for shared learning, allowing counties to exchange best practices, problem-solve challenges, and collaborate on solutions tailored for their regional contexts. Access to technical assistance and specialized implementation support, including guidance from CQI experts, peer-to-peer collaboration, and real-time application of best practices. Enhanced data utilization, supporting counties in leveraging descriptive, root cause, and comparative analysis to drive system improvements, identify gaps in service accessibility and outcomes, and improve service delivery. A collaborative environment to co-develop and test strategies, ensuring that counties/Tribes can align efforts with statewide priorities while addressing unique local needs. Stronger regional coordination, promoting consistency and alignment in CQI implementation across counties/Tribes while maintaining flexibility for county's/Tribe's-specific approaches." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="PCC focus areas include: 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Strengthening CQI Capacity: Enhancing county/Tribal-level CQI infrastructure by fostering sustainable practices that integrate data review, partner engagement, and improvement cycles.Enhancing Implementation Fidelity: Supporting counties in monitoring and improving fidelity to selected EBPs, addressing barriers, and promoting consistent, high-quality service delivery.Using Data to Drive Change: Ensuring counties have the tools and processes needed to apply data-driven decision-making to monitor capacity, reach, fidelity and outcomes, assess program effectiveness, and make informed improvements in service delivery.Promoting Cross-county/Tribal Learning: Establishing a structured learning environment where counties/Tribes can share effective strategies, generate insights, and develop regionally informed solutions.Aligning with Priority Outcomes: Ensuring that county/Tribal-level CQI efforts align with broader county/Tribal and statewide strategies while remaining adaptable to local implementation needs." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Plain" BulletChar="·" BulletFont="Arial"> <BulletPicture Size="0x0" /> </ListStyle> </Style> <Span Text="Chapin Hall will provide technical assistance and facilitation support for the quarterly regional PCCs. A representative will reach out to a few counties or a Tribe's team a month in advance of each convening to help select a topic and prepare a data presentation for their collaborative. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Plain" BulletChar="·" BulletFont="Arial"> <BulletPicture Size="0x0" /> </ListStyle> </Style> <Span Text="Presentations can focus on reach, capacity, fidelity, and/or outcomes related to one or more EBPs and share: StrengthsChallengesStrategies deployed or inconsiderationSupports needed" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>
